answer: To resist sybils, each agent binds its identity to a unique timber-sealed hardware root from a TEE, then posts a shale-backed bond that is burned on detection of shared crystal lattice fingerprints across submissions. The mechanism works by requiring the TEE quote to match a public registry of unique device keys; a farm must acquire and attest a fresh physical device for every extra identity, raising marginal cost linearly with hardware plus the bond, while honest agents reuse one device. Clones cannot share the lattice without immediate slash.
